cues: Most adjectives can stand in two places: before the noun, a tall boy, or after a linking verb, the boy is tall.
Afraid, alive, asleep, alone, aware and their family only come after the verb: the child was asleep, but never the asleep child; say the sleeping child.
And main, only, mere, former, latter and elder only come before the noun: my elder brother, but never he is elder than me; say older.
text: Most adjectives can stand in two places: before the noun, a tall boy, or after a linking verb, the boy is tall. But a few are fixed. Afraid, alive, asleep, alone, aware and their family only come after the verb: the child was asleep, but never the asleep child; say the sleeping child. And main, only, mere, former, latter and elder only come before the noun: my elder brother, but never he is elder than me; say older.
